column1: # mutation-slow-suites.tsv — paired suites measured at or above 5s in the canonical
# environment. The PR lane defers any guard whose killer appears here.
# Membership drift is a report warn, never red; this committed copy updates by ordinary PR.
# A paired suite ABSENT from this file is treated as fast.
# selftest<TAB>seconds<TAB>measured_at   (seconds from the seed run's unmutated precheck; ISO-8601 date)
# The two 2026-08-06 rows are NOT from a seed run — they are serial, unloaded macOS
# measurements taken while diagnosing a PR-lane step timeout (#413). Both suites clear the 5s
# membership criterion by a wide margin on any platform, which is the only thing membership
# turns on; the SECONDS are a local observation and the next seed run should overwrite them.
# Their absence was the timeout: `lean-gate.sh` and `check-lean-chain.sh` were being swept on
# the PR lane as though their killers were fast, and a diff touching both (plus three more
# guards) enumerated 53 mutants against a 38s and a 16s suite. Deferral is what the lane's
# time bound is made of, and it could not fire on data that did not exist.
